Welcome. Thank you. Good afternoon, Chairman McKay and members of the board. The Fairfax County Sheriff's Office is your public safety team, and we take great pride in the exceptional services we provide to the county.

I appreciate the county executives' proposed budget changes to our starting pay grade and longevity steps.

Unfortunately, this funding is not enough to make our agency competitive in today's law enforcement professional job market. With a vacancy rate of 26%, I have made numerous cutbacks that affect not only my agency, but also the residents of Fairfax County.
Since September of 2022, the following changes have been made. Mandatory overtime for staff during FY 2023 at a cost of $6.9 million. We anticipate the estimated cost of $8.3 million this year.

To further illustrate, we average seven to nine deputies working overtime each shift to ensure the safety of the adult detention center. These overtime assignments are hours. These deputies should spend at home with their family.

Captains and first lieutenants have been working overtime in operational positions that are designated for sergeant or private first class. I closed the alternative incarceration branch, which has left our judiciary without any sentencing alternatives, such as work release, home incarceration, and electric monitoring, and the fines option program.

I suspended the community labor force. I modified operations at the prisoner intake area to accommodate staffing shortages, leading to longer wait times for officers and their arrestees. Currently, all divisions within the sheriff's office are below recommended staffing levels.

Staff attrition has increased due to comparably low pay, mandatory overtime, and quite frankly, a general feeling of being unappreciated.

Jail population has risen, in part due to the closure of jail alternatives previously provided by the Alternative Incarceration Branch. We are forecasted to reach a vacancy rate of 30% by the end of the calendar year, and further cutbacks, such as removing my staff from the Sharon Boulevard Center for Community Health and Code Compliance, are likely to occur.

Increased pay for current and future sworn employees would have a tremendous effect on my agency's ability to return to full staffing and to continue to operate at the highest level, just as we always have. Increased pay would promote retention and also current employees by compensating them commensurate with the important work they perform.
